---
title: "Set up"
---

## Files

```sh
git clone https://github.com/corne00/dynamic-gxe-workshop.git
cd dynamic-gxe-workshop
```

`R/functions.R` contains all functions used in the workshop, and `python/dgxe.py` the same functions in Python. `data/` contains the Narrabri weather and the biomass trajectories.

## Language

Every code block is available in R and in Python. Selecting a language in any of the tabs switches all code on the page, and the choice is remembered. Printed output and figures are produced by the R code; the Python code gives the same numbers (coefficients and errors agree to three decimals, up to the convergence tolerance of the penalised methods).

## Packages

R 4.1 or later. The fitting methods use `glmnet` and `leaps`; the interpretation page uses `iml` (with `yaImpute`); the figures use `ggplot2`.

```r
install.packages(c("glmnet", "leaps", "ggplot2", "iml"))
```

Python 3.9 or later with `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy`, `scikit-learn` and `matplotlib`; the interpretation page also uses `PyALE`. Python is run from the repository root with `python/` on the path.

```sh
pip install numpy pandas scipy scikit-learn matplotlib PyALE
export PYTHONPATH=python
```

## Test run

```r
source("R/functions.R")

wx <- read.csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv")
traj <- read.csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz")

drv <- make_drivers(wx)
Theta <- make_library(drv)
tr <- make_trajectories(traj, drv)

P <- cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit_ols, genotypes = tr$genotypes[1:20])
round(evaluate(P, tr), 3)
```

```python
import pandas as pd
from dgxe import *

wx = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv")
traj = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz")

drv = make_drivers(wx)
Theta = make_library(drv)
tr = make_trajectories(traj, drv)

P = cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit_ols, tr.genotypes[:20])
print(evaluate(P, tr))
```

The result is the root-mean-square error (t/ha) of 20 genotypes on seasons that were left out of the fit; it should take a few seconds.
